newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU favours direct Helms-Burton settlement with U.S.
newsitem.headline: EU favours direct Helms-Burton settlement with U.S.

text.p: The European Union said on Monday it would rather resolve differences with the U.S. over its anti-Cuba legislation directly with Washington than have the World Trade Organisation (WTO) rule on the matter.
Diplomats said EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels expressed regret that talks with the U.S. over its Helms-Burton Act showed deep differences remained.
In a statement, EU foreign ministers expressed their willingness to "continue to seek an overall bilateral settlement and in that case to halt or suspend the panel procedure" at the WTO.
The act -- an culmination of years of U.S. policy aimed at isolating the Cuban government of Fidel Castro -- was passed last year to a chorus of indignation from the EU and other American allies.

Among other things it allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts any foreign companies and individuals deemed to have gained from investments in property confiscated by the Cuban government since the communist revolution of 1959.

Although this part of the legislation has twice been suspended by President Bill Clinton, the EU is also opposed to another section which prohibits foreigners with links to companies investing in confiscated property from entering the U.S.

Last week WTO chief Renato Ruggiero named a three-person panel to adjudicate on the matter, but Washington said it would not cooperate and reserved its right to invoke a little-used "national security clause" in its defence.
Earlier, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind told reporters the EU continud to believe the U.S. had a case to answer.
"I don't think there are legitimate national security considerations, but we shall have to wait and see," he said.
